Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I put together a concise implementation plan focused on the three items we agreed are highest impact for BlueSky's storefront summarization workload:

- KV prefetch / prefix caching to avoid repeated tokenizer & KV warm-up on short-lived sessions
- Batching configuration tuned to 50–150ms latency SLOs for your interactive queries
- Quantization profile selection (we'll test q4f16 and q8_0 for tradeoffs) and a safe rollback route

I've attached a one-sheet checklist that maps owners, timeline, and acceptance criteria (see implementation-checklist.xlsx). High-level asks for this week:
1) Confirm whether customer data will route through your VPC or use hosted path (important for routing policy and audit logs).
2) Share a representative sample of 250 requests (anonymized) so we can produce a prefetched KV hit-rate simulation.
3) Pick a 60-minute window for the initial integration call — we recommend Dec 15 or 16 morning PST.

Deliverables from Redwood by Dec 17: perf baseline, recommended batch parameters per endpoint, and two pre-built quant profiles for A/B testing.

If that's aligned I'll add Monica (implementation lead) and Rishi (quant lead) to the working calendar invite.

Thanks,

Team —

Notes from quick pre-call triage (technical bullets we should bring to kickoff):

1) Prefetch/Cache strategy-  Plan: implement prefix-level KV caching at the routing tier. For short sessions we should prepopulate the KV with top-10 probable prefixes per session (sampled from provided corpus). Target: >70% KV hit rate in first 5 tokens. Fallback: if miss rate >40% under load, switch to no-prefetch and use micro-batches.

2) Batching policy-  Target latency SLO 50–150ms for interactive queries. Start with dynamic batching window of 12–48ms with max batch size 16 for the smallest model variant; increase to 32 for larger variants. We'll add a conservative concurrency cap at the gateway to avoid queueing. Metrics to monitor: token latency p50/p95, queue time, batch size distribution.

3) Quantization profiles-  Propose two candidate profiles for A/B: q4f16 (best latency with slight quality delta) and q8_0 (higher fidelity, higher cost). Rishi: prepare a micro-benchmark comparing generation perplexity and ROUGE on the provided sample. Also plan an automated rollback policy: if quality metric drops >6% or hallucination rate increases beyond threshold, route 100% to non-quantized variant.

4) Routing policy & VPC notes-  Because BlueSky will route through their VPC, ensure we provide a routing policy that pins sensitive endpoints to dedicated nodes and writes audit logs to their KMS-backed store. Need specific VLAN/peer IPs from their infra team in advance.

5) Observability & acceptance-  For acceptance: baseline tokens/sec, end-to-end p95 latency, and KV hit rate. Monica will own test harness and acceptance run; Vivek will own rollout automation (canary percentages + auto-fallback).

I've attached the updated quant profile spec and a sample prefetch log for the team to review (quant-profiles-v2.pdf, sample-prefetch-log.txt).

Action items before kickoff:
- Rishi: run the q4f16 vs q8_0 microbench by EOD Wed (12/15).
- Vivek: prep route templates and canary playbook.
- Sofia: confirm calendar and send pre-kickoff pack to BlueSky.
